newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WMC shuts nickel mine after accident.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WMC shuts nickel mine after accident.

text.p: WMC Ltd stopped production and evacuated workers from its Rocky's Reward nickel mine in Western Australia late on Wednesday after a miner was killed in a rockfall, a company spokesman said on Thursday.

The mine, part of WMC's Leinster mining complex located 370 km northeast of Kalgoorlie, will remain closed pending investigations by WMC, local authorities and the dead miner's contract employer Eltin Contracting, the spokesman said.
About 850,000 tonnes of ore is mined annually from Rocky's Reward, accounting for about 45 percent of the 30,000 tonnes of nickel metal processed from the Leinster complex, he said.
"We did stop operations in the mine at the mine," he said adding it was too early to determine how long the mine would be closed. "The investigation is still occurring," he said.
The miner had been working at a depth of about 210 meters below the surface when he was struck by rocks, he said.
Safety concerns at WMC mines were highlighed in the company's annual report released this week, which cited the deaths of four workers in 1995/96 to June 30.
WMC last year formed an "Elimination of Fatalities" taskforce to improve safety procedures.
